config.title: Pumpkin Patch in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Where to pick your own pumpkin in Berlin, which pumpkin shows and festivals are worth the trip, and which ticket you need.

items.q: Is there a pumpkin patch in Berlin where you can pick your own?
items.a: Yes, but only one weekend a year inside the city. The **Erntefest at Domäne Dahlem** opens its pumpkin field on **Saturday 3 and Sunday 4 October 2026**, 10:00 to 18:00, and harvesting stops at 17:00. You get a harvest sack for a €2 deposit and pay at the field tills.

items.q: How much does the Domäne Dahlem pumpkin harvest cost?
items.a: Entry is **€4.50**, €2 reduced, and children under 12 go in free. The pumpkins you pick are paid for separately at the field tills, and the farm lists cash payment.

items.q: What is the biggest pumpkin show near Berlin?
items.a: The **Spargel- und Erlebnishof Klaistow** near Beelitz, with more than 100,000 pumpkins built into figures. It is open daily 9:00 to 18:00 until 15 November, costs **€6 at weekends** and €4 on weekdays, and children under 12 are free.

items.q: Where can I see pumpkins in Berlin for free?
items.a: The pumpkin show at the **Späth'sche Baumschulen** in Baumschulenweg is free to walk around until early November, and you buy pumpkins by weight in the farm shop. **Karls in Elstal** is also free to enter and keeps its pumpkin season until 1 November.

items.q: Which pumpkin places can I reach with a Berlin ABC ticket?
items.a: Domäne Dahlem and Späth are in zone AB, and Karls in Elstal and the Fredersdorf festival are in ABC. **Klaistow and Kremmen lie outside ABC**, so you need a ticket to that zone or the Deutschlandticket.

items.q: When are the pumpkin festivals around Berlin in October?
items.a: **Kremmen** holds its Kürbisfest in the historic barn quarter on **17 and 18 October**, 10:00 to 18:00. **Fredersdorf** has a village pumpkin festival with a bonfire on **Saturday 24 October** from 15:00, with free entry.

items.q: Where do I throw away my Halloween pumpkin in Berlin?
items.a: In the **brown Biotonne**, the organic waste bin in your courtyard, like any other vegetable scraps. Cut a large pumpkin into pieces first.
